title: Quantification of Global Diastolic Function by Kinematic Modeling-based Analysis of Transmitral Flow via the Parametrized Diastolic Filling Formalism
protocol: Record a complete 2D/echo-Doppler study for all subjects.
Position subjects in the supine position.
Obtain apical four-chamber views using a 2.5 MHz transducer.
Gate the sample volume at 1.5-5 mm directed between the tips of the mitral valve leaflets.
Set the wall filter at 1 (125 Hz) or 2 (250 Hz).
Adjust the baseline to take advantage of the full height of the display.
Adjust the velocity scale to exploit the dynamic range of the output without aliasing.
Perform Doppler tissue imaging with the sample volume gated at 2.5 mm.
Position the sample volume at the lateral and septal portions of the mitral annulus.
Save Doppler examinations in DICOM format.
Record Doppler examinations on DVD with simultaneously recorded electrocardiogram (ECG).
Convert images from the DICOM format and video to bitmap (.bmp) files using a custom MATLAB program.
Load the bitmap image files on another custom MATLAB program.
Measure conventional transmitral flow parameters such as Epeak, Apeak, Edur, E’peak, A’peak, etc.
Crop the images for PDF analysis.
Select images with discernible transmitral flow contour and complete cardiac cycle indicated by ECG for analysis.
Mark the time sampling rate (measured in pixels/s on the horizontal axis) in the images.
Mark the velocity sampling rate (measured in pixels/(m/sec) along the vertical axis) in the images.
Identify the complete cardiac cycle by noting consecutive R peaks on the image.
Mark the transmitral Doppler E- and A-wave or tissue Doppler E’- and A’-wave in the selected cardiac cycle.
Select the Doppler E-wave peak point (Epeak) or E’-wave peak point.
Mark the start of the wave using the line connecting the peak to the start as a guide for matching the acceleration slope of the E-wave or E’-wave.
Calculate the interval from the start to peak flow, denoted as the E-wave or E’-wave acceleration time (AT).
Mark the end of the E-wave or E’-wave using the line connecting the peak to the end as a guide for matching the deceleration slope.
Calculate the interval from the peak to the baseline, denoted as the deceleration time (DT).
Determine the duration of the E-wave by calculating the sum of AT and DT (Edur = AT + DT).
Mark the A-wave using a similar procedure as used for the E-wave.
With both the E- and A-waves marked, calculate the Epeak/Apeak ratio.
Load the cropped image into the custom LabView program.
Set the threshold such that MVE approximates transmitral flow.
Select onset and termination points of MVE along the time-axis by the operator.
Input user-selected MVE points to the computer program for fitting.
